patient.chief_complaint: Wife called 911 - husband convulsing 20 minutes after missing yesterday's dialysis session
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Brown is a 61-year-old African American man with ESRD on hemodialysis who is brought by ambulance in active status epilepticus after his wife called 911. She reports he missed his scheduled dialysis session yesterday due to transportation issues. He last had dialysis 4 days ago (his Monday session was missed and it is now Wednesday). He had been feeling increasingly confused and nauseated over the past 24 hours. He developed a generalized tonic-clonic seizure approximately 20 minutes ago that has not stopped. He has no prior history of seizures or epilepsy. His wife reports he drank significantly more fluids than usual yesterday because he felt thirsty.

output.proposed: Calcium gluconate 1g IV for K+ 6.8 cardiac stabilization; insulin-dextrose for K+ lowering; emergency dialysis
warnings: K+ 6.8 is a cardiac emergency - calcium gluconate 1g IV IMMEDIATELY for membrane stabilization
Then insulin 10 units + D50W 50 mL IV to shift K+ intracellularly (transient)

DEFINITIVE treatment: emergency dialysis - only way to truly remove K+ in ESRD
Levetiracetam for SE: ESRD dose adjustment required - max 500-1000 mg twice daily (normal is 1500 mg BID); give supplemental dose after dialysis
Avoid phenytoin in ESRD - highly protein-bound, altered free fraction; use with caution
Amlodipine: hold during active SE management

output.query: Antiepileptic drug dosing ESRD hemodialysis AED pharmacokinetics renal failure

results.finding: Levetiracetam: primarily renally cleared; dose adjustment in ESRD - max 500-1000 mg twice daily; give supplemental 250-500 mg after each dialysis session
Lacosamide: 50% renally cleared; reduce dose to 200-300 mg/day in ESRD; supplemental dose after dialysis
Phenytoin: highly protein-bound; in ESRD, protein binding reduced, free fraction increased; interpret levels carefully - measure free phenytoin
Valproate: primarily hepatically metabolized; safer in ESRD but monitor ammonia and platelet count
Topiramate: primarily renally excreted; halve dose in ESRD

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Uremic status epilepticus from missed hemodialysis with severe metabolic derangement (BUN 142, K 6.8, Ca 6.8, Na 128) in ESRD

differential.key_features: K 6.8, Ca 6.8 are themselves seizure-provocative; uremia is the unifying cause

Uremia causes platelet dysfunction; CT to exclude SDH

differential.key_features: Drug accumulation in ESRD can lower seizure threshold; renal AED dosing essential

useless_tools.rationale: No clinical suspicion of cardiac source of embolus or cardiogenic seizure; routine echo is not indicated in SE workup absent cardiac findings.
No suspicion of arrhythmogenic syncope or cardiac comorbidity precipitating SE; routine telemetry beyond standard ICU monitoring adds cost without yield.
Amyloid PET has no role in acute SE evaluation; dementia biomarker imaging does not change acute management.
Carotid duplex is for ischemic stroke workup; SE without focal vascular suspicion does not warrant carotid imaging.
DaTscan / dopamine transporter imaging has no role in SE; no parkinsonism question relevant to acute management.
Uremia explains presentation; LP not indicated initially.

sequence_constraints.reason: ECG hyperkalemia changes must be reviewed before calcium gluconate and other K-lowering therapy.
Confirm K, Ca, BUN before urgent dialysis ordering and AED dosing.

critical_actions: Urgent hyperkalemia treatment: calcium gluconate IV, insulin + dextrose, bicarbonate, sodium polystyrene
Emergent hemodialysis — definitive treatment for uremic SE
Load IV levetiracetam with renal dose adjustment
contraindicated_actions: Do NOT use renal-cleared AEDs at standard doses
Do NOT use sodium phosphate / IV magnesium without dialysis ready
Avoid IV phosphate or magnesium supplements without dialysis; will worsen retention in ESRD.
key_reasoning_points: Missed dialysis with BUN 142 and severe electrolyte derangement (K, Ca, Na) is a layered SE precipitant — uremia, hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia, hyponatremia each contribute
Emergent hemodialysis is the definitive treatment
AED dosing requires renal adjustment in ESRD
Uremic platelet dysfunction increases SDH risk — CT essential
